$comment: R1770 — `$at` is the SURFACE EXTENT this canon was written against, and
this screen's own paint sweep reads it from here rather than declaring a
size of its own. See `analyzer-inspector-spec.json` for what a pin that
named no size cost this tool.
R1730 — the analysis tool's KEY PATTERN section, written down once, in
neutral vocabulary, as the behaviour reference draws it.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A RUST CONSTANT. The same reason
`analyzer-rail-spec.json` is one, applied a level down. The screen's own
`spec` module is what a RUNNING screen needs — paint tags, column widths,
row data, the wording of a refusal. If the specification lived beside it,
written by the same hand in the same edit, a conformance test would be
asking the thing under test for the answer.
EXTRACTION. The reference is not in this repository and must not be. The
procedure is recorded in the session memory note on the behaviour
reference: the section is one method producing the rows, one producing the
detail, and one block of markup drawing both. Measured 2026-08-19: seven
columns in one order, a 320-wide detail pane with eleven parts, and a
46-high section header carrying a name, a derived summary and a filter box.
VOCABULARY. The reference's product, protocol and resource words are
replaced by the words the tool class uses generally. Structure and
behaviour are what is being reproduced; the wording is not. Two titles
below name a part the reference draws WITHOUT a label — `standing` and
`summary` — and one, `pattern`, labels the pane's subject line. Those three
titles are this file's words for what is there, and the file says so rather
than pretending the reference wrote them.
THE TWO HALVES. Each surface carries `canon` — what the reference has — and
`owed` — where this build does not have it, each entry carrying the round
that accepted it and why. The gate asserts the difference between the built
surface and `canon` is EXACTLY `owed`, so a new divergence fails and so
does an owed one that has been paid off without this file being told.
The section header the reference draws across the top of the list, 46
high: what the section is called, how much is in it, and the box that
narrows it. The summary is DERIVED in the reference too — it counts the
rows and the ones needing attention — so a build that hard-codes the
sentence has not reproduced it.
The list's columns, left to right. The reference fixes six widths and
lets the pattern take the rest, which is the column a reader is actually
reading — so the widths are the screen's and the ORDER is the
specification's.
The 320-wide pane on the right, top to bottom. It is a record rendered as
labelled parts rather than a tree, which is what distinguishes it from
the capture viewer's decode pane: four of its parts are a two-by-two grid
of single facts, one is a chip list, and the last is an action that
leaves the section.
`declarer` is drawn by the reference as a live button leading to its
topology section. The scope reference draws that section LOCKED — it is
booked under a requirement of a later release, which is what
`analyzer-rail-spec.json` records — so reproducing the affordance
faithfully means drawing it and refusing it with that reason. Leaving it
off would be a divergence; making it navigate would be a promise the
specification does not keep.
